title: I couldn’t find the cozy game I wanted on my phone, so I made one (pixel-art farm, no ads, portrait)
author: BodybuilderHorror304
selftext:
Hi there, solo dev here, and this is the first game I’ve ever released.

I’ve been pretty nostalgic lately for the games I grew up with. You’d open them and just play. No account to create, no “special offer” popping up the moment it loads, no ad every time you harvest something. I spent hundreds of hours in Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing and I wanted something like that on my phone, a game I could play for five minutes on the bus or for a whole evening on the couch. I couldn’t really find one, so I ended up making it. Honestly I made it for myself first.

In **Pixel Farm** you grow crops, you fish, you dig in the mine and you raise animals. You can donate your fish and fossils to the aquarium and the museum and watch them grow. There’s a forge where you craft pretty much everything (better rods and pickaxes, jewelry, furniture...). And you can decorate and expand your house, from a tent all the way to a big estate with a veranda. The farm also follows your phone’s calendar and clock, so you get the real seasons and the shift from day to night, which makes it really cozy.

The farm keeps going while you’re away, and when you come back the game tells you what it produced. Your crops don’t die if you forget about them for a few days.

A couple of things I want to be upfront about. **There are no ads at all, not even the “watch a video to double your harvest” kind.** You can finish the whole game for free. There’s a gem shop if you want to go faster, but nothing in it is locked behind paying.

Also, I’m not a programmer. I designed the game myself (the mechanics, the economy, the story, all the balancing) but the code was made using AI. I know it’s a sensitive topic, but to me that’s what’s exciting about it: people with an idea and a lot of passion can now make the game they’ve always wanted. And I have a full-time job, so I’m not doing this for the money. The shop is mostly there to cover the costs (Apple’s fees, the servers that keep your save, etc.).

It’s iPhone only for now, Android is planned, and it’s in English and French. If you’re in the EU it’s not available yet because Apple is still checking my company’s paperwork, should be a matter of days.

I’d really love your feedback, especially on the first 10 minutes or so. I’ll be around in the comments all day!

https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6797645042

comments.author: CloudsSpeakInArt
comments.body:
Played it for a little bit, here are some notes I took while playing the beginning

\-Some of the pop up animations feel a bit overdone, especially when catching your first fish  
\-It seems like when tapping on a location on the home tab, it acts like it's opening a "new menu" and makes the app feel a little too much like it's in a browser if that makes sense, like you can pull the left of the screen to go to previous  
\-I don't know if it's because accuracy leads to better catches, but fishing feels way too easy, all I have to do is tap the screen when there's a tug and there's a lot of grace time  
\-I wish the soundtrack looped properly instead of reverbing back to the beginning awkwardly  
\-Art style is pretty nice  
\-Performance seems flawless, iPhone 16 Pro
